## Investments and Newcastle

Reviewed 11 September 2026. Use the relevant disposal, income, or NSW assessment year. Newcastle fee ranges remain unverified.

91. Which expenses can I claim for a rental property?

Separate rental income, private use, borrowing costs, repairs and capital items before claiming expenses.

- Gather agent statements, invoices, loan interest, ownership details and rental availability records.
- Apportion costs where required and reconcile the deduction schedule to the supporting documents.

The treatment depends on the expense and property use; a rental label alone does not establish deductibility.

Property and land

Link to question 91

92. Is work on my rental property a repair, an improvement or a depreciating asset?

Review what the work did to the property and when the relevant damage or condition arose.

- Keep invoices, scope of work, purchase condition and dates; split distinct components where supported.
- Assess repair, capital works and depreciating asset treatment separately and update the relevant schedules.

Cost alone does not distinguish a repair from an improvement or initial repair.

Property and land

Link to question 92

93. How do I work out the capital gain when I sell an investment property?

Build the capital gains calculation from the relevant event, proceeds and adjusted cost base.

- Gather purchase and sale contracts, costs, ownership and occupancy history, and capital works records.
- Review any exemptions, adjustments, residency and discount conditions before calculating the net result.

A sale price minus purchase price calculation can omit material tax adjustments.

Capital gains tax · Experimental tax worksheets and supported years

Link to question 93

94. How do capital losses and the CGT discount affect tax on shares I sell?

Calculate each gain or loss, apply eligible capital losses, then consider any available discount.

- Retain trade records, cost base adjustments, holding periods and carried-forward loss balances.
- Reconcile the final calculation to the year's CGT schedule and keep the remaining loss record.

The bounded worksheet assumes the gains, losses and discount eligibility have already been established.

Capital gains tax · Experimental tax worksheets and supported years

Link to question 94

95. Do I owe tax when I sell, swap or spend cryptocurrency?

Review each crypto disposal and income event, including swaps and spending, rather than only withdrawals to cash.

- Export exchange and wallet activity, fees and Australian dollar values with dates.
- Reconcile transfers between your own wallets separately from transactions that require tax review.

The tax treatment depends on the activity and event; this site does not import wallets or classify transactions.

Crypto asset investments

Link to question 95

96. How do I report ETF distributions and their tax adjustments?

Use the fund's annual tax statement and any AMMA statement to reconcile the distribution components.

- Match cash, reinvestments, capital gains, foreign income and credits to the statement.
- Record cost base increases or decreases and carry them into the investment register.

Cash received alone can differ from the amount and components that belong in the tax return.

Investments and assets

Link to question 96

97. What records does my accountant need for an SMSF annual return and audit?

Prepare the financial records and trustee evidence needed for both the return and the independent audit.

- Gather bank and investment records, valuations, contributions, pensions, minutes, member balances and supporting agreements.
- Reconcile opening and closing balances and resolve the auditor's record requests before finalising the return.

This checklist does not perform an SMSF audit or certify compliance.

ATO self-managed super funds

Link to question 97

98. When does an investment property become liable for land tax in NSW?

Check ownership, land values, exemptions and any surcharge conditions for the relevant NSW land tax year.

- Reconcile all relevant NSW landholdings, ownership interests and valuation notices.
- Use Revenue NSW's current assessment guidance and retain the calculation and exemption evidence.

Purchase price and one property's value alone do not establish the full land tax position.

Land tax

Link to question 98

99. How much does an accountant or bookkeeper cost for a small business in Newcastle?

Compare written quotes for the same Newcastle bookkeeping or accounting scope. The research did not establish a reliable local fee range.

- Specify transaction volume, payroll headcount, entities, BAS frequency, cleanup needs and reports.
- Compare inclusions, software, GST, setup fees, review frequency and work charged separately.

This personal open source site does not quote for professional engagements.

TPB register of tax and BAS agents

Link to question 99

100. How do I choose a Newcastle accountant who can help with Xero and cash flow reporting?

Shortlist providers against the work you need and verify the relevant registrations.

- Check the TPB register for tax or BAS services, and ask who prepares and reviews the work.
- Request a sample reporting pack, Xero experience, cash forecast process, responsibilities and a written scope.

Location or software certification alone does not demonstrate the quality of advice or forecasting.

TPB register of tax and BAS agents

# GST calculator: exclusive, inclusive and GST amounts

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/gst/

> Enter an amount with or without GST and get the GST component, the exclusive amount and the inclusive amount at 10%, rounded once to cents, in your browser.

# GST calculator

Work out GST, the GST-exclusive amount and the GST-inclusive amount for a wholly taxable supply at 10%, rounded once to cents.

One of the nine business calculators. Calculations run in this browser. The calculator code does not send your inputs to a server or save them automatically.

Planning estimates in AUD. Confirm tax treatment, liability amounts and dates separately. Amounts round to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded up.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

JavaScript is required for interactive calculations. The formula, assumptions and source links remain available below.

## GST

For a wholly taxable amount at 10% GST, exclusive amount / 10 gives GST; inclusive amount / 11 gives its GST component. Each result rounds once to cents. Mixed, GST-free and input-taxed supplies need classification first.

Eligible cost × supported business use percentage / 100. This apportions the amount you supply. It does not determine deductibility, depreciation or record sufficiency.

# Margin and markup calculator

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/margin/

> Work out gross profit, margin and markup from sales and direct cost in your browser, on a consistent GST basis. A zero denominator leaves that percentage undefined.

# Margin and markup calculator

Gross profit, margin and markup from sales and direct cost, on a consistent GST basis and matching period.

One of the nine business calculators. Calculations run in this browser. The calculator code does not send your inputs to a server or save them automatically.

Planning estimates in AUD. Confirm tax treatment, liability amounts and dates separately. Amounts round to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded up.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

JavaScript is required for interactive calculations. The formula, assumptions and source links remain available below.

## Margin and markup

Gross profit = sales − direct cost. Margin = gross profit / sales × 100. Markup = gross profit / direct cost × 100. Use a consistent GST basis and matching period. A zero denominator leaves that percentage undefined.

# Break-even sales calculator: units and sales

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/break-even/

> Work out contribution per unit, break-even units (rounded up) and break-even sales from fixed costs, price and variable cost per unit, in your browser.

# Break-even sales calculator

Whole units and sales required to cover fixed costs from price and variable cost per unit.

One of the nine business calculators. Calculations run in this browser. The calculator code does not send your inputs to a server or save them automatically.

Planning estimates in AUD. Confirm tax treatment, liability amounts and dates separately. Amounts round to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded up.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

JavaScript is required for interactive calculations. The formula, assumptions and source links remain available below.

## Break-even sales

Contribution per unit = price − variable cost per unit. Required units = fixed costs / contribution, rounded up. Required sales = whole units × price. Use one product or a stable representative mix and a consistent GST basis.

# Hourly pricing calculator for a required rate

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/hourly/

# Hourly pricing calculator

Required hourly rate before GST from annual costs, target profit and billable hours.

One of the nine business calculators. Calculations run in this browser. The calculator code does not send your inputs to a server or save them automatically.

## Hourly pricing

# Budget variance calculator: favourable or unfavourable

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/variance/

> Compare actual to budget for an income or cost line in your browser: the difference, its percentage of absolute budget, and whether it is favourable or unfavourable.

# Budget variance calculator

Actual minus budget, the percentage of absolute budget, and whether the difference is favourable or unfavourable.

One of the nine business calculators. Calculations run in this browser. The calculator code does not send your inputs to a server or save them automatically.

Planning estimates in AUD. Confirm tax treatment, liability amounts and dates separately. Amounts round to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded up.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

JavaScript is required for interactive calculations. The formula, assumptions and source links remain available below.

## Budget variance

Difference = actual − budget. Percentage = difference / absolute budget × 100. A zero budget has no percentage comparison. Positive income differences are favourable; positive cost differences are unfavourable. Explain causes from the records.

Budget explanation checklist

Monthly Close Controls compares trial balance CSVs and lists material movements for review.

# Monthly loan payment calculator

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/loan/

> Estimate a fixed monthly loan payment, first-month interest and principal, and total interest from principal, annual rate and term, in your browser.

# Monthly loan payment calculator

Fixed monthly payment, first-payment interest and principal, and estimated total interest, with no fees or balloon.

One of the nine business calculators. Calculations run in this browser. The calculator code does not send your inputs to a server or save them automatically.

Planning estimates in AUD. Confirm tax treatment, liability amounts and dates separately. Amounts round to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded up; loan estimates allow for calculation precision.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

JavaScript is required for interactive calculations. The formula, assumptions and source links remain available below.

## Monthly loan payments

For fixed monthly interest r and n payments: payment = principal × r / (1 − (1 + r) raised to −n). At zero interest, payment = principal / n. Payments are in arrears, with no fees or balloon. Interest is estimated from unrounded payments; lender rounding and daily accrual can differ.

# Staff cost calculator: annual and monthly

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/staff/

> Add wages, the super amount you supply and other annual costs to see the annual and monthly cost of a staff member, in your browser, with nothing counted twice.

# Staff cost calculator

Annual and monthly cost of a staff member from wages, the supplied super amount and other annual costs.

## Staff cost

Annual cost = wages + supplied super amount + other annual costs. Monthly average = annual cost / 12. Include expected insurance, payroll tax, recruitment, relief staff and equipment in other costs. Paid leave already within salary must not be added again.

# 13-week cash forecast calculator with CSV export

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/business-calculators/cash/

> Build a 13-week cash forecast in your browser: weekly closing cash, one delayed receipt, the funding gap against a buffer, CSV export and saved inputs.

# 13-week cash forecast

Weekly closing cash from opening cash, receipts and payments, with one delayed receipt and a funding gap against a buffer. Save, load and export as CSV.

One of the nine business calculators. Calculations run in this browser. The calculator code does not send your inputs to a server or save them automatically. Use Save inputs to download a local scenario file, then Load inputs to resume it.

Planning estimates in AUD. Confirm tax treatment, liability amounts and dates separately. Amounts round to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded up.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

JavaScript is required for interactive calculations. The formula, assumptions and source links remain available below.

## 13-week cash forecast

Weekly closing cash = opening cash + receipts − payments. Each closing balance opens the next week. Funding gap = minimum buffer − lowest opening or weekly closing cash, with a floor of zero. It is a planning gap, not a lending decision. Weekly totals can hide a shortage within the week.

business.gov.au: cash flow

The Lumbridge cash flow case works the same question with a 45-day receipt delay.

13-week cash forecast inputs

First day of week 1 Load inputs (replaces the current forecast)

Save inputs to a file on your device and load it to continue later. File contents are processed in your browser. A valid file replaces all forecast inputs; an invalid file leaves them intact. Each week covers 7 days from the start date.

Save inputs

Opening bank balance (AUD) Minimum cash buffer (AUD) Original receipt week Receipt to delay (AUD) Delay in whole weeks

Enter bank receipts and payments for each week, including GST where cash includes it. Include BAS, payroll, super, loan payments, capital purchases and drawings in their expected payment weeks. The initial zeros are empty planning amounts. A delayed receipt must already be included in the original week's total.

# Privacy and site use

Source: https://duguid.com.au/privacy/

> How duguid.com.au handles browser calculations, cookies, hosting and feedback, with the site's advice boundaries and software licence links.

# Privacy and site use

This notice explains how this website handles browser calculations, hosting and feedback.

Published 12 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

## Browser calculations

The website's calculators process the figures you enter in your browser. They do not send those figures to a server or save them in browser storage. Download any results you want to keep before leaving the page. Downloaded files stay wherever you save them.

The accounting-question search also runs in your browser. It does not send search text to a search service. It does place the search term and topic in the page address so a filtered list can be bookmarked or shared, which means the term appears in your browser history and in any address you pass on.

## Cookies and analytics

The website's own code does not set cookies or include advertising pixels. Its fonts, images, and application scripts are served from this domain.

No analytics script is delivered. Cloudflare Web Analytics was removed from this site on 20 September 2026, so the site owner receives no page-view reports. GitHub Pages and Cloudflare still process requests to host and protect the site, as the Hosting section below describes.

Email Address Obfuscation is disabled so email links work without scripts. The address is public in the HTML pages, their plain-text alternates, and the machine-readable index. The contact page also spells it out for anyone whose browser does not open an email app.

Cloudflare also asks browsers to report network errors to Cloudflare for seven days and to prefetch pages you are likely to open next (the nel, report-to and speculation-rules response headers). Neither carries the figures you type into the calculators. A prefetched or shared page address can carry question-search terms, because the search places them in the address; do not put confidential information in a search you may share or leave in your history.

Cloudflare also supplies visitor-verification code as part of page delivery. Both additions are made after the files leave this website's source and are served from this domain. Cloudflare may process technical request and browser-verification information and may set its own security cookies; see Cloudflare's cookie documentation. That processing is separate from the figures the calculators handle, which their own code works out in your browser without sending them to a server.

When you select Human or Machine view, your browser saves that display preference on this device. The preference is not sent to a server. You can change it with the view switch or remove it by clearing this site's browser storage.

## Hosting

GitHub Pages hosts this website's files, and Cloudflare delivers them to your browser. These providers process technical information about visits, which may include IP addresses, request details, and security or performance data. See the GitHub Privacy Statement and Cloudflare Privacy Policy for their handling of that information.

## Feedback and external links

If you email me, I receive your email address and the content you send. Use fabricated examples when reporting a problem. Do not include taxpayer information, client files or other confidential records. An email stays in my mailbox until I delete it, GitHub keeps issues public in its own systems under its terms, and I cannot delete copies other people hold.

GitHub issues are public. Links to GitHub and other websites take you to services with their own privacy policies. Software you download or install has its own documented data handling; this notice covers the website.

For questions about this notice or information you have sent me, email ryan@duguid.com.au. To ask what personal information I hold, have it corrected, or complain about how I handled it, email that address, or take a complaint about the handling of personal information to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner. Other project links are on the Contact page.

## AI crawlers and citation

The site's robots.txt names each crawler and its treatment. Search indexing and the fetches an assistant makes to answer or cite for a user are allowed for the agents it names, and Google-Extended is allowed so Gemini grounding can cite the site. Common Crawl (CCBot) and Bytespider are allowed to crawl the open web, while the closed-lab training crawlers it names, GPTBot and ClaudeBot among them, are disallowed. The machine-readable index and the full page text are published for citation, and robots.txt is the current policy if this summary and the file ever differ.

If an AI answer misquotes this site, email ryan@duguid.com.au with the page address and the quoted text. Use fabricated examples only; do not send client records or taxpayer information.

## Using this site

Read the advice and review boundary and the site boundary before relying on a tool or example. Check each page's assumptions, source links and review date, and have a qualified professional review outputs before acting on them.

The website source is available under its MIT licence, which includes its warranty terms. Linked projects and third-party assets carry their own licences. Check those terms before reusing or distributing them.

# Profit vs cash flow: an Australian Excel worked example

Source: https://duguid.com.au/examples/profit-vs-cash-flow/

> A fictional Newcastle business holds quarterly profit at $35,957.55 AUD while one late $44,000 receipt leaves cash $25,160 short. Workbook, figures and limits.

# Profit vs cash flow: an Australian Excel worked example

How can a business report a profit and still run short of cash? Because profit records the sale and cash records the day the money arrives. This worked example moves one receipt by 45 days: quarterly profit stays at $35,957.55 and the bank account falls $25,160 below zero.

Download the Excel example Compare the two cases

XLSX, 23,506 bytes. Needs desktop Excel with automatic calculation. The explanation and results below can be read without Excel.

Lumbridge Services is fictional. Every business, customer, invoice, balance and date here is fabricated, and all amounts are Australian dollars (AUD). No client outcome is described.

Published 18 September 2026. Last reviewed 21 September 2026.

## The business and the question

Lumbridge Services is a fictional maintenance business in Newcastle, New South Wales. It bills two service lines, Varrock maintenance and Falador repairs, and invoices $60,000 of work each month: $40,000 Varrock and $20,000 Falador, before GST. The forecast covers the quarter from 1 October to 31 December 2026.

The owner wants to buy equipment. The quarter shows a profit, so the money looks available. The question is whether the bank account can carry the business to the end of December if one customer pays late.

The model holds every other assumption still. Monthly materials are $12,000 and overhead $6,000. Gross wages are $24,000 a month, with $19,000 paid to employees, $5,000 of PAYG withholding and $2,880 of super. The opening bank balance, receivables, payables, GST, loan and tax instalment all come from fabricated 30 September 2026 balances. The owner's policy is to keep $15,000 in the bank.

## The one change: a 45-day delay

Invoice OPEN-V is September work for the Varrock line: $40,000 plus $4,000 GST, so $44,000 is banked. The baseline case receives it on 14 October 2026. The late case receives the same $44,000 on 28 November 2026, 45 calendar days later.

Nothing else changes. The work was performed in September either way, the invoice was issued either way, and the customer pays in full either way. Only the day the money lands moves.

The workbook exposes that single control. Assumptions!B2 holds the delay in whole calendar days and accepts 0 to 120. Every figure below is the model's own output at 0 and at 45.

## Both cases, side by side

Same work, same customer, different receipt date. All amounts AUD. Scroll sideways on small screens.

Forecast measure | Receipt on time | Receipt 45 days late
Quarter revenue | $180,000.00 | $180,000.00
Profit before income tax | $35,957.55 | $35,957.55
October customer receipts | $66,000.00 | $22,000.00
October closing cash | $32,040.00 | ($11,960.00)
First day the bank account is negative | None in the quarter | 28 October 2026
Lowest daily closing cash | $16,800.00 on 7 October | ($25,160.00) on 6 November
December closing cash | $67,320.00 | $67,320.00

The two cases end the quarter with the same cash because the delayed receipt still arrives, on 28 November. That later recovery cannot pay the wages, supplier invoices and GST that fall due in late October and early November.

Against the owner's $15,000 buffer, the late case is $40,160 short at its worst day. A reader looking only at December closing cash, or only at profit, sees neither the shortfall nor its date.

Weekly closing cash in the late case, exported from the distributed workbook in Excel 16.0 on 13 September 2026. The 13 plotted values are $16,800, $15,600, $25,520, ($11,960), ($11,960), ($25,160), $17,640, $27,560, $49,680, $36,480, $79,280, $67,320 and $67,320, against the assumed $15,000 buffer. Capture record.

## Why profit did not move

Profit is measured on the accrual basis. Lumbridge earned the OPEN-V revenue when it performed the work in September, so the sale sits in the September accounts in both cases. Moving the receipt changes the debtor balance, not the revenue, and no expense changes either. Quarterly profit before income tax is $11,985.85 a month in both cases, or $35,957.55 for the quarter.

Cash is measured on the day money moves. The payments the business owes do not wait for a customer. In the late case October receipts fall from $66,000 to $22,000, while the same $63,960 of payments still leaves the account, including materials on 7 October, the September-quarter GST of $12,600 and a $3,000 income tax instalment on 28 October, and net wages and super on 28 October.

The model states the bridge between the two. It starts from profit, adds back depreciation of $200 a month and the non-cash leave provision of $2,254.15 a month, adjusts for the movement in gross receivables and the GST liability, then subtracts the $1,000 monthly loan principal and the tax instalment. A separate direct cash schedule ties to that bridge exactly: the model's reconciliation difference is $0.00 in every month of both cases.

Three obligations are still outstanding at 31 December in both cases: $12,600 of GST, $5,000 of PAYG withholding and $13,200 of supplier invoices. The $67,320 closing balance is not spendable surplus.

## The decision for a person

The model does not approve or refuse the equipment purchase. It gives a reviewer three things to act on:

- Confirm the OPEN-V receipt date with the customer before committing to discretionary spending.
- Resolve the funding gap between 28 October and mid-November, which the model neither borrows nor overdraws. No overdraft, new loan or owner contribution is assumed anywhere in this forecast.
- Compare actual collections with the forecast each week, because the whole result turns on one date.

Whether the business should defer the purchase, arrange finance or accept the risk is a judgement about a real business with real customers. This example supplies the arithmetic, not that judgement.

## Open the workbook

Needs desktop Excel with automatic calculation. No Xero login, add-in, macro or AI agent is used, and the workbook contains no macros and no external links.

- Download the synthetic Excel forecast (23,506 bytes).
- Download the sample pack: the same workbook, the 6 source files, model notes, the management briefing, the trial guide, the fixed CSV exports and the source MIT licence.
- Read the sample record for the source commit, hash and verification.
- Open the Model and Cash 13 weeks sheets and find quarterly profit and December closing cash.
- Change Assumptions!B2 from 0 to 45. Trace invoice OPEN-V and watch the lowest daily balance and its date.
- Restore 0, then save a copy and reopen it to confirm the original figures return.

Only the workbook recalculates. The briefing, the CSV exports and the JSON summary in the sample pack are fixed exports taken at a 0-day delay: editing the workbook does not rewrite them. Rebuild from source with the matching delay when you need an export and a workbook that agree.

## Rebuild it from source

The example lives in the au-fpa-pack repository, an Australian extension of Jeff Brines / Guiderail's openfpa. From a checkout of the captured commit, with Python 3.11 and uv:

```
uv sync --locked --extra dev
uv run --locked --extra dev python examples/lumbridge-services/models/generated/lumbridge.py
uv run --locked --extra dev python examples/lumbridge-services/models/generated/lumbridge.py --delay-days 45
```

Each run writes the workbook, briefing and schedules to examples/lumbridge-services/output/ and verifies all 21 monthly workbook lines against the Python model before replacing the workbook. Expect quarter_profit_before_tax of 35957.55 in both runs, and minimum_daily_cash of 16800.0 on 2026-10-07 at a 0-day delay and -25160.0 on 2026-11-06 at 45. A rebuilt workbook can differ in package metadata or cache bytes from the file distributed here.

Read the source and assumptions at the captured commit.

## Provenance and verification

- Source. au-fpa-pack at commit 386c7ff. The example is part of that repository, not of the published au-fpa-pack v0.1.1 distribution, so the commit rather than the release identifies it.
- Distributed workbook. SHA-256 b150de6281fccb6dcb1d221c034b047eb610ad4064972c5d9ac9fca8916b8463, 23,506 bytes. Its model and all 6 input files match the captured source after normalising line endings.
- Formula check. A fresh check on 11 September 2026 passed all 21 monthly workbook lines against the Python model, and the repository's offline suite passed.
- Native Excel record. The file distributed here is the exact workbook from the original native check, dated 11 September 2026, which exercised 116 cells and 13 chart values per case at 0, 45 and 100-day delays, plus invalid input bounds, formula errors and save-and-reopen behaviour. That record covers this artefact and that scenario control only.
- Maintainer trial. On 14 September 2026 Ryan Duguid reported that the workbook worked in Microsoft 365 Excel, including the 0 to 45 to 0 sequence and saving and reopening. The exact Excel build and individual figures were not recorded in that report.

## Limits

This is a fabricated demonstration, not advice and not a client result. No forecast accuracy, client outcome or time saving has been measured.

- The only supported scenario is the receipt delay, from 0 to 120 whole calendar days. Revenue, wages and operating assumptions are fixed.
- Payment dates, PAYG withholding, workers compensation, the tax instalment and the loan terms are supplied scenario assumptions, not statutory calculations. PAYG withholding is a flat $5,000 a month, not a withholding table result.
- Payroll tax is nil because annualised wages and super of $322,560 sit below the bundled $1.2 million New South Wales threshold for a single ungrouped employer. Grouping and interstate wages need separate assessment.
- Daily balances net everything dated on the same day. They do not establish intraday liquidity or the order in which payments clear.
- The output is not a complete forecast statutory balance sheet, and it does not calculate company income tax expense.
- The example does not test when a super fund receives a contribution. Payday Super timing covers that question.

Varrock and Falador are Old School RuneScape naming references. No game assets or prices are used, and no affiliation with Jagex is claimed. No game knowledge is needed.

## Common questions

### How can a business make a profit and still run out of cash?

Profit records revenue when the work is performed and cash records money when it arrives. In this example the September work stays in September profit whether the $44,000 invoice is banked on 14 October or 28 November, so a 45-day delay leaves quarterly profit at $35,957.55 while the bank account falls to minus $25,160 on 6 November.

### What changes between the two cases?

One date. Invoice OPEN-V, worth $40,000 plus $4,000 GST, is received on 14 October 2026 in the baseline and on 28 November 2026 in the late case. Revenue, expenses, wages, supplier terms and every other payment date are identical.

### Why do both cases end December with the same cash?

The delayed receipt still arrives inside the quarter, on 28 November, so both cases close December at $67,320. The recovery is too late to fund the payments due in late October and early November, which is why the daily view matters more than the closing balance.

### Is this a real client case?

No. Lumbridge Services, its customers, invoices and balances are fabricated. No client outcome, forecast accuracy or time saving is claimed.

# Ozzit: Excel LAMBDA functions for Australian financial modelling

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/ozzit/

> A free Excel workbook of 133 native LAMBDA functions and 5 help tables for Australian modelling: GST, financial years, AASB 16 leases and amortisation.

# Ozzit: Excel LAMBDA functions for Australian financial modelling

Download Ozzit from GitHub Try a formula

Needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 and later. Choose ozzit.xlsx under Assets on the release page.

Ozzit is a single Excel workbook holding 133 native LAMBDA functions and 5 named help tables, all under the oz. prefix. It covers amortisation, depreciation, ratios, AASB 16 lessee schedules and Australian GST and financial year helpers. There is no add-in, no macro and no external dependency: the functions are ordinary defined names you can read and copy.

Current release v3.4.2, published 20 September 2026, verified 20 September 2026. Release record and verification on GitHub.

Published 18 September 2026. Last reviewed 20 September 2026.

## What Ozzit is

An Excel workbook, not a program. Open it, copy a function into your own model, and the formula travels with the file. Every definition is a native LAMBDA stored as a defined name, so the arithmetic stays inside the workbook where a reviewer can read it.

The v3.4.2 workbook carries 138 named formulas: 133 LAMBDA functions and 5 help tables that document them inside the workbook. Each module also ships an editable demonstration worksheet, and the formula source is published as plain text in the repository's src/ folder and indexed in functions.csv.

The Australian helpers are deliberately small: GST addition and extraction at 10%, a 1 July financial year label, 2 modelling depreciation schedules and 4 AASB 16 lessee schedules. The rest of the library is general financial modelling.

## Who it is for and what it needs

It suits an accountant or analyst who builds models in Excel and wants the working visible rather than hidden in an add-in or a macro. It is not a bookkeeping tool, and it never touches a ledger.

What the workbook needs. Scroll sideways on small screens.

Requires | Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 and later, with LAMBDA and dynamic arrays
Does not run in | LibreOffice and Excel versions before 2024, which cannot evaluate the functions
Contains | No VBA, no macros, no add-in and no external link
Licence | MIT, covering the workbook, the formula source and the function index
Author | Ryan Duguid. Built from scratch, with provenance recorded in the repository

## Selected functions

Ten of the 133, with their published signatures. The full index is in functions.csv.

Selected functions from the v3.4.2 index. Scroll sideways on small screens.

Function | Signature | What it returns
oz.GSTExtractλ | (Amounts, [Rate]) | The GST contained in GST-inclusive amounts
oz.GSTAddλ | (Amounts, [Rate]) | GST added to GST-exclusive amounts
oz.FinancialYearλ | (Dates, [StartMonth]) | The Australian financial year a date falls in, starting 1 July
oz.PrimeCostλ | (Cost, Life) | A straight-line depreciation schedule in whole years
oz.DiminishingValueλ | (Cost, Life) | A diminishing-balance schedule at 200% of the straight-line rate
oz.Amortiseλ | (Principals, APRs, Terms, StartDates, [Timeline]) | A corkscrew amortisation schedule
oz.LeaseLiabilityλ | (Payments, Rate, [InAdvance]) | Present value of lease payments unpaid at commencement
oz.PeriodRateλ | (AnnualRate, [PeriodsPerYear]) | An effective annual rate converted to a rate per period
oz.DayCountRateλ | (Timeline, APR, [Convention], [EndDates]) | A period rate under 30/360, Actual/360, Actual/365 or Actual/Actual
oz.IRRλ | (Values, Dates) | IRR corrected for a first investment outside the first period

## One worked example

Take $1,100 that is assumed to be wholly taxable and GST-inclusive at 10%. Enter this formula in a cell of the Ozzit workbook:

```
=oz.GSTExtractλ(1100)
```

The result is 100.00. Check: 1100 / 11 = 100.00.

That is the whole of the function's contribution: 10% arithmetic on an amount you supply.

Whether the supply is wholly taxable, whether a tax invoice supports it and whether the credit is claimable in that period are decisions for the reviewer. The function cannot see the evidence and does not classify the supply.

The repository records a native Excel capture of this example, including the formula read back from the cell and the returned value. That capture was taken in release v3.2.0, an earlier and different workbook file, so it certifies the example in v3.2.0 rather than in v3.4.2. The v3.4.2 gate results below are the record for the current file.

## Download and use it

Needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 and later. Nothing is installed.

- Open the v3.4.2 release page and download ozzit.xlsx from its assets. The release also publishes SHA256SUMS and a provenance record.
- Check the file before you trust it: the v3.4.2 asset is 439,097 bytes with SHA-256 0306793a7e473ce70e78149fea1e107fc0f714d61ab50960c16f6fd528878f6f.
- Read the source, guides and changelog, or start with the guide to opening the workbook and copying functions.

To use a function in your own file, copy the cell that calls it, or copy the definition from the workbook's name manager into your model. The function then belongs to your workbook and stays with it. Cite the library with the metadata in the v3.4.2 CITATION.cff, which names the release this page documents. The default branch may already carry a later version.

## Release verification

Release v3.4.2 was built from a signed tag and gated before publication. On 20 September 2026, in Excel 16.0 build 20430:

- 1,129 formulas recalculated with 0 in error.
- 905 assertions ran with 0 failures: 603 written by hand, 23 of them randomised against independent formulas, and 302 generated from the workbook's own help.
- 19,444 cached values were confirmed to equal what their formulas produce.
- 246 unit tests passed, and the published formula source reproduced all 138 named formulas.

Those checks establish that the workbook calculates what its definitions say. They do not establish that a given accounting treatment is correct.

## Limits

Not tax, legal or financial advice. The functions calculate; a person decides the accounting treatment and signs off.

- The GST helpers do 10% arithmetic only. They do not classify a supply, test registration or prepare a BAS.
- oz.PrimeCostλ and oz.DiminishingValueλ are modelling schedules. They are not ATO Division 40 methods and they do not implement immediate write-off or low-value pools.
- The AASB 16 functions are lessee arithmetic. They do not decide the lease term, what counts as a lease payment, or whether an arrangement contains a lease, and they do not cover lessor accounting or the short-term and low-value exemptions.
- The library contains no individual income tax, Medicare levy, Division 7A interest or tax rate cards.
- The 13-week cash flow workbook in the repository's templates folder is a separate template, not a function in this library.
- Known defects are listed in the repository's changelog and issues. Check a schedule against an independent calculation before relying on it.

## Common questions

### What is Ozzit?

An Excel workbook containing 133 native LAMBDA functions and 5 help tables for financial modelling under Australian conventions, published free under the MIT licence. It has no add-in, macro or external dependency.

### Which Excel versions can run it?

Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 and later, which support LAMBDA and dynamic arrays. LibreOffice and earlier Excel versions cannot evaluate the functions.

### Does Ozzit calculate Australian tax?

No. It performs 10% GST arithmetic and labels Australian financial years, and its depreciation and lease functions are modelling schedules rather than ATO or standard-setting methods. It contains no income tax, Medicare levy or Division 7A calculations.

### Where do I get the current release?

Release v3.4.2, published on 20 September 2026, ships ozzit.xlsx with a SHA256SUMS file and a provenance record on its GitHub release page. Compare the downloaded file's SHA-256 with the published value before use.
